metadata.description: A design system for geographical data visualization inspired by ancient Chinese maps and academic archives. Features parchment backgrounds, faint boundary lines, and distinct geometric markers in jade and cinnabar tones.

background.description: Aged parchment or raw silk color. Serves as the base for the entire map.

mapElements.description: Faint, slightly lighter beige/off-white used for regional borders. Must be subtle to not overpower data points.

text.description: Primary text is a dark brownish-grey (ink black faded over time). Accent titles and dividers are muted cinnabar red.

dataMarkers.description: Muted, natural mineral colors used for data points. Jade for primary categorizations, Rust for secondary or distinct subsets.

fontFamilies.description: Traditional brush-style or serif typography is mandatory. Sans-serif breaks the historical immersion.

sizes.description: Size scaling is used to represent quantitative data (e.g., scale or dimensions).

bullseye.description: Used for highly significant or protected data points.

backgroundWatermark.description: A very faint background illustration of traditional architecture (roofs, brackets) underlying the map to give a sense of topic and texture.

promptRules: 1. VISUAL HIERARCHY: Data markers are the most prominent elements. Map boundaries must be very faint (low contrast against the parchment background).

2. MARKER RENDERING: When generating map points using HTML/SVG, use distinct SVG shapes (`<circle>`, `<polygon>` for triangles/pentagons/squares) filled with either `$colors.dataMarkers.jadeGreen` or `$colors.dataMarkers.rustRed`.

3. LEGEND CONSTRUCTION: The legend should be a floating card over the map. Use thin red lines (`$colors.text.accentTitle`) to separate different categorization logic (e.g., shape logic vs. color logic vs. size logic).
4. TYPOGRAPHY: Force CSS to use 'KaiTi', 'STKaiti', or generic 'serif' for all text.
5. NO PURE COLORS: Never use #000000, #FFFFFF, pure red (#FF0000), or pure green (#00FF00). Stick strictly to the mineral and earth tones defined in the palette.
